question: In the Waymo product lessons episode, why did Shweta Shrivastava advise product managers to prioritize company impact over maneuvering for promotion, and what should they focus on instead?
expected_points: Promotion-focused maneuvering can be noticed and viewed negatively, and it distracts from important work.
Build product-management skills and seek challenging, high-visibility work that stretches those skills.
Stay dedicated to work that has business impact for the company.

answer.summary: Shrivastava advised focusing on meaningful company impact rather than trying to engineer a promotion: conspicuous maneuvering can send a negative signal and distract from the work. Instead, build PM skills, make your interest in challenging work known, and commit to projects that serve the business.

sections.heading: Why prioritize impact
sections.content: She said trying too hard to maneuver for promotion can become visible and send the organization a negative signal. It can also distract from the work that deserves attention. Her advice was to focus on impact; she framed promotion as a result of having impact and doing what is right, rather than pursuing the promotion too intensely.

sections.heading: What to focus on instead
sections.content: Improve your product-management skillset, let your manager or leader know you want challenging, high-visibility projects that stretch your skills, and then dedicate yourself to the work. Prioritize what has business impact for the company and do the right things for that cause.

sections.heading: Why prioritize impact over promotion tactics
sections.content: Shrivastava’s view was that trying too hard to maneuver for promotion can be noticed by the organization and send a negative signal. It also distracts PMs from what they should be focused on: creating the right impact for the company and doing what is right for the business.

sections.heading: What to focus on instead
sections.content: Improve your product-management skillset, make your interest in challenging, high-visibility projects known to your manager, and then commit to work that stretches your skills and has business impact. She did not advise hiding ambition: letting a manager know can help them consider you when the right opportunity arises.

The evidence says to improve product-management skills and pursue challenging, high-visibility projects that test or stretch those skills. The answer includes these recommendations.
The evidence says to focus on the right company impact and work with business impact. The answer clearly says to prioritize company impact and commit to work with business impact.

answer.summary: Shrivastava cautioned that overly maneuvering for promotion can be visible as self-serving and distract from the work. Instead, focus on company impact, strengthen your PM skills, and take on challenging work that stretches you and advances the business. [S1, S2]

sections.heading: Why not maneuver for promotion
sections.content: She said that trying too hard to position yourself for promotion can become visible and send a negative signal to the organization; it can also distract you from what you should be focusing on. Her framing was that the way to get promoted is not to want it too badly, but to focus on impact and doing what is right for the company. [S1, S2]

sections.heading: What to focus on instead
sections.content: Improve your product-management skillset, make your manager or leader aware that you want challenging, high-visibility work that will stretch your skills, and then commit to that work. Prioritize what creates business impact for the company and do the right things. [S1]
